questions.title: Elastic collision of two balls — momentum, acceleration & distance

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Momentum is the product of the mass and the velocity of an object (p = mv).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
a = Δv/Δt = (−0.8 − 1.6)/(0.12 − 0.09) = −2.4/0.03
magnitude of acceleration = 80 m s⁻² (read-offs from Fig. 1.1: v = +1.6 m s⁻¹ at t = 0.09 s, v = −0.8 m s⁻¹ at t = 0.12 s)

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
Δp = mΔv = 0.15 × (−0.8 − 1.6) = 0.15 × (−2.4)
magnitude of change in momentum = 0.36 kg m s⁻¹

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer:
Distance = area under the v–t graph during the collision (t = 0.09 s to 0.12 s):
½ × 1.6 × 0.020 + ½ × 0.8 × 0.010 = 0.016 + 0.004
distance = 0.020 m

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer:
For an elastic collision, the relative speed of approach equals the relative speed of separation.
Speed of approach = 1.6 − 0 = 1.6 m s⁻¹, so speed of separation = v(Y) − (−0.8) = v(Y) + 0.8 = 1.6
velocity of Y = +0.80 m s⁻¹

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: Sketch on Fig. 1.1: a horizontal line at v = 0 from t = 0 to t = 0.09 s; a straight diagonal line of positive gradient from (0.09 s, 0) to (0.12 s, +0.80 m s⁻¹); then a horizontal line at +0.80 m s⁻¹ from t = 0.12 s to t = 0.20 s.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.answer:
Conservation of momentum on the frictionless surface (no external horizontal force):
0.15 × 1.6 = 0.15 × (−0.8) + 0.80m
0.24 = −0.12 + 0.80m → 0.80m = 0.36
mass of Y = 0.45 kg

questions.title: Suspended polythene thread — Young modulus & elastic energy

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The Young modulus of a material is the ratio of stress to strain (stress per unit strain), within the limit of proportionality.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
Stress = F/A, where F = weight of the whole thread = mg = 0.018 × 9.81 N
σ = (0.018 × 9.81)/(2.6×10⁻⁶) = 0.177/2.6×10⁻⁶
stress = 6.8×10⁴ Pa

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer: The weight supported at a point decreases linearly as the distance from the top increases, because less thread hangs below the point. Since the cross-sectional area is uniform, stress (σ = F/A) is proportional to the weight supported, so the variation is linear.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer:
E = ½Fx, with F = σA = 6.8×10⁴ × 2.6×10⁻⁶ = 0.177 N
E = ½ × 0.177 × 6.1×10⁻⁴
elastic potential energy = 5.4×10⁻⁵ J

parts.label: (d)
parts.answer: The total extension is less — in the vertical thread the stress is less than 6.8×10⁴ Pa everywhere except at the very top (the stress, and hence the extension per unit length, is smaller lower down the thread).

questions.title: Double-slit interference — coherent light, fringes & frequency

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: When two or more waves meet (overlap) at a point, the resultant displacement at that point is the sum of the individual displacements of the waves.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: Waves are coherent if they have a constant phase difference.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: The light diffracts (spreads out) as it passes through each slit.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer: The waves from the two slits meet (superpose) at X with zero path difference / zero phase difference (they are in phase). Constructive interference occurs, so the resultant wave has maximum amplitude, forming the bright fringe.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.answer:
λ = ax/D → x = λD/a
x = (560×10⁻⁹ × 0.43)/(1.4×10⁻⁵) = 2.41×10⁻⁷/1.4×10⁻⁵ = 1.72×10⁻² m (fringe spacing)
The first dark fringe lies halfway between the central maximum and the first bright fringe:
XY = x/2 = 1.72×10⁻²/2 = 8.6×10⁻³ m

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: Mark a cross B at the next bright fringe — the same distance above Y as XY, i.e. one fringe spacing (2XY) above X.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: Mark a cross D at the first dark fringe below X — the same distance below X as XY.

parts.label: (d)
parts.answer:
c = fλ → f = c/λ
f = (3.00×10⁸)/(560×10⁻⁹)
frequency = 5.4×10¹⁴ Hz

questions.title: LDR across a cell — internal resistance & power

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Draw a cell symbol with the internal resistance shown (a resistor symbol in series inside a dotted box around the cell, or just the cell symbol); the LDR symbol connected across the terminals of the cell (in parallel with it); and a voltmeter symbol connected in parallel with the LDR.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: A zero error / calibration error of the digital voltmeter (or contact resistance in the connections / resistance of the connecting wires).

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.answer: As the light intensity decreases: the resistance of the LDR increases; the current in the cell decreases; the p.d. across the LDR increases (V = E − Ir, with E and r fixed, so less p.d. is dropped across r).

questions.title: Mesons, quarks & β+ decay — conservation and neutrino

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: A meson is a hadron consisting of one quark and one antiquark.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer:
Quark charges have magnitudes of either ⅔e or ⅓e.
Charge −1e: any two of — three quarks each of charge −⅓e (e.g. ddd); two quarks of charge −⅔e plus one quark of charge +⅓e.
Charge +2e: three quarks each of charge +⅔e (e.g. uuu).

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer:
Conserving nucleon number and charge (proton number) in ¹⁸₈X → ᴾQY + ʳₛβ⁺ + ⁰₀Z:
P = 18, Q = 7 (proton number of X decreases by 1 in β⁺ decay), R = 0, S = +1 (the positron has charge +1e and negligible mass).

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: Particle Z is the (electron) neutrino.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.answer: In β⁺ decay a proton changes into a neutron, so the net change in quark composition is an up quark changing to a down quark (uud → udd).

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.answer: The total energy released in each decay is constant, but particle Z takes some of this energy — the energy is shared between Z and the β⁺ particle. The way the total energy is distributed between them varies from decay to decay, so the β⁺ particles have a continuous range of kinetic energies.
